title: Smallest Square Fitting N Rectangles
statement:
You have `n` identical rectangles, each of width `w` and height `h`. You want to place all of them inside one square without overlaps. Rectangles **cannot be rotated**: every rectangle keeps its width along the same side of the square. Rectangles are laid out in a grid of rows and columns.

Find the minimum side length of a square that can hold all `n` rectangles. Since `w` and `h` are integers, the answer is an integer.

**Follow-up:** the obvious solution tries side lengths one by one. Can you do much better by exploiting the fact that if a side length works, every larger side length works too?
inputFormat: A single line containing three integers `n`, `w` and `h`.
outputFormat: Print the minimum side length of the square.

examples.explanation: With side 8 the grid has 4 columns and 2 rows, which holds only 8 rectangles. With side 9 it has 4 columns and 3 rows, which holds 12 ≥ 10, so 9 is the smallest.
A single rectangle needs a square at least as large as its longer side.
Side 6 fits a 2 x 2 grid of 3 x 3 rectangles; side 5 fits only one per row and column.

hints: For a square of side s, the grid holds floor(s / w) columns and floor(s / h) rows, so it fits floor(s / w) * floor(s / h) rectangles.
That count never decreases as s grows, so the set of valid sides is a suffix: binary search on s.

A safe upper bound is n * max(w, h) (put them all in one line). Beware that the product of the two floors can overflow 64-bit integers for large s; stop comparing as soon as it reaches n or divide instead of multiplying.
